name: Papaya extract
lead: Papaya extract is a preparation from the fruit, leaves, seeds or latex of Carica papaya. In skincare it is usually described as an enzyme exfoliant, because papaya latex is the source of the protein-digesting enzyme papain.[1]

Papain is used in meat tenderizers, enzymatic wound debridement products and dental caries gels.[1] No human trial of papaya extract for skin appearance was found; published research covers other uses, including a systematic review of papaya extract in dengue, and animal and in vitro studies.[2][3]

In 2008 the US FDA warned companies to stop marketing topical papain drug products, citing reports of hypersensitivity reactions, and latex-allergic people may be at higher risk of reacting to papaya.[1]

paras: Papain (EC 3.4.22.2) is collected as latex from scored papaya fruit, dried and purified. It is used in leather, cosmetic, textile, detergent, food and pharmaceutical industries.[1]

No studies found for skin appearance. Related human evidence concerns other uses: a 2019 systematic review and meta-analysis examined papaya leaf extract in dengue fever.[2] Other work is in animals, such as rat studies of leaf extract on blood glucose and 28-day toxicity,[3][4] and a polyurethane nanofiber burn dressing loaded with honey and papaya extract tested in vitro for hemocompatibility.[5]

The FDA's 2008 warning on topical papain products followed reports of hypersensitivity reactions with hypotension and tachycardia, and the agency advised concerned users to consult a healthcare provider.[1]

card.summary: Papaya-derived enzyme exfoliant botanical; no skin-appearance trials found and the FDA warned on topical papain drug products in 2008.
card.note: Possible allergy risk, particularly for people with latex allergy.

quick.overview:
Papaya extract is used in skincare mainly as an enzyme exfoliant because papaya latex contains papain, a protein-digesting enzyme.

No human trial for skin appearance was found; research is on other uses and in animals.
quick.mechanism: Papain breaks down proteins, which is the basis for exfoliation and wound-debridement uses.
quick.risks: The FDA warned in 2008 about topical papain drug products after hypersensitivity reports. People allergic to latex may also react to papaya.
